claims.claim: The same self-recursive loop explains salvation, coherence, and why God cannot be proven from inside the system.
claims.plain_english: One single idea—a loop that refers back to itself—can explain how people are saved, how things make sense, and why you can't prove God exists using only the rules inside the universe.
claims.evidence_given: The document asserts this as the central thesis but provides no formal proof or derivation in this interlude; it directs readers to a canonical page for the full argument.
claims.what_would_break_it: If salvation, coherence, and unprovability each required fundamentally different explanations, or if a non-recursive model could explain all three more simply.

claims.claim: The framework introduces a new category that binds science and theology.
claims.plain_english: There is a new way of thinking that connects science and religion into one system.
claims.evidence_given: The document repeats this claim as a pull quote and verdict but does not define the category or show how it binds the two domains.
claims.what_would_break_it: If science and theology remain irreconcilable under this category, or if the category is shown to be a re-labeling of existing concepts without new explanatory power.

claims.claim: God cannot be proven from inside the system.
claims.plain_english: You can't use logic or evidence that comes only from within the universe to prove that God exists.
claims.evidence_given: The document states this as a consequence of the self-recursive structure but does not provide a formal proof in this interlude.
claims.what_would_break_it: If a valid logical proof of God's existence were constructed using only premises internal to the system, or if the system itself were shown to be incomplete in a way that allows external proof.

claims.claim: The self-recursive structure is the load-bearing structure of the framework.
claims.plain_english: The idea that something refers back to itself is the main support holding up the whole theory.
claims.evidence_given: The document names this structure but does not explain how it bears weight or why it is necessary.
claims.what_would_break_it: If the framework could be restructured without recursion, or if recursion leads to paradoxes that invalidate the framework.

claims.claim: The interlude sends the reader to the canonical page instead of replacing it.
claims.plain_english: This short version is just a preview; the real, complete explanation is on another page.
claims.evidence_given: The document explicitly states this and provides a link to the canonical page.
claims.what_would_break_it: If the canonical page did not exist or did not contain the promised full argument.

claims.plain_english: The idea of a self-referencing loop is the key to understanding how people are saved.
claims.evidence_given: The document asserts this as part of the thesis but provides no theological argument or scriptural support in this interlude.
claims.what_would_break_it: If salvation is shown to require a non-recursive mechanism, or if the loop cannot account for key theological doctrines like atonement or grace.

claims.plain_english: The self-referencing loop is also the reason things make sense and fit together.
claims.evidence_given: The document states this but does not define coherence or show how recursion produces it.
claims.what_would_break_it: If coherence can be explained without recursion, or if recursion leads to contradictions that undermine coherence.
